html:
Georgetown is the capital and chief port of Guyana, at the mouth of the Demerara River. It was laid out in the 1780s and named Stabroek by the Dutch, then renamed Georgetown by the British in 1812.

The town lies below the level of high tide, protected by a sea wall and drained by canals and sluices, a Dutch way of building carried over from the colonial plantations. Its wide streets are lined with wooden buildings, among them St George's Cathedral, one of the tallest wooden churches in the world.

It grew as the trading town of British Guiana, exporting sugar, rum and timber. Most of the country's people live on the narrow coast near it. Georgetown has the 1763 Monument to the Berbice revolt and was the seat of independent Guyana from 1966.
